title: House of Tocco
capsule: The Tocco were an Angevin-aligned Italian dynasty that acquired the County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos in 1357, when Robert of Taranto granted the islands to Leonardo I Tocco. The dynasty reached its apex under Carlo I Tocco (d. 1429), who captured Ioannina in 1411 and Arta in 1416, earning the Byzantine title of Despot from Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos and controlling much of Epirus. Ottoman pressure progressively stripped mainland holdings after 1449; Leonardo III Tocco, the last count, was driven from the islands in 1479. Venice absorbed Zakynthos in 1484 and Cephalonia with Ithaca in 1500, extinguishing Latin lordship over the Ionian Islands.

Island territories are clearly delineated; mainland Epirote holdings fluctuated substantially and their exact extents at any given year are reconstructed from chronicle sources rather than cartographic evidence.
